expected_effect: No action is proposed, so no change in any metric or log stream should be observed as a result of this proposal. The next observable step is diagnostic, not remedial: a pod listing for the social-network namespace and a relaxed Loki selector (namespace-only, or label-based rather than guessed pod-name regex) would show whether nginx-thrift and compose-post-service pods exist, are Running, and are shipping any lines at all. That query returning named, running pods with log output - or returning no pods at all - is the observation that would let a real remediation be chosen.
if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if the incident is in fact an ongoing hard outage that any of the three available actions would clear, and the delay costs availability. The observation that would show that: a relaxed-selector Loki query or nginx exporter surfacing a repeating upstream error (connection refused / host not found naming a nginx-thrift upstream), or a pod listing showing nginx-web-server in CrashLoopBackOff with a climbing restart count. Either would meet restart_service's precondition (process state) or point at the freshly created ConfigMap's upstream names, and the proposal should be reopened immediately. Note also that the effect of any fix here is hard to observe: span metrics are structurally absent for both nginx-web-server and compose-post-service [tr_81d3c68dcd9a][tr_00357570b0e6], so error-ratio recovery cannot be measured - confirmation would have to come from access logs or an exporter, which is itself a reason not to act blind.
risk: The risk of abstaining is continued outage if one is in progress. The risk of the alternative - acting anyway - is concrete and is why I decline: rollback_image has no prior image tag because the workload is recorded as first created, not redeployed [tr_1808ab6d2147], so it would redeploy to nothing; revert_config has no prior configuration because the nginx-thrift ConfigMap and Service were created rather than updated and no earlier version exists in the 24h window [tr_1808ab6d2147], so a revert would delete or blank working-or-not routing config with no known-good state to return to; restart_service requires evidence pointing at process state, and every process-state signal on this board is unavailable-or-unvalidated rather than negative [tr_81d3c68dcd9a][tr_ce237924350e][tr_c626ef4ef205][tr_4b6926841b8a], so a restart would be a coin flip that destroys the current container state irreversibly and erases exactly the startup evidence needed to answer whether the 07:02 bootstrap completed.
blast_radius: None, since nothing is executed. Had an action been taken on nginx-web-server, it is the ingress for this slice and its callers are every external client of the social-network frontend; compose-post-service, home-timeline-service and user-timeline-service sit behind it and would see traffic stop for the duration of any container recreate. A restart of nginx-web-server in particular is irreversible per the action's own terms and would be visible to every user-facing request path at once.
